summary: In this excerpt from a novel's Book 6, Arthur and the narrator speak with Checker, who is tracking Professor Sonya's phone and has suggested bringing in authorities such as the NSA because of a threatening note. Arthur asks for twenty-four hours before deciding whether to make the call himself. The conversation then turns to Pilar, whom the narrator has armed with a gun, which upsets Arthur.
one_line: Arthur and the narrator debate involving the NSA over a threat to Professor Sonya, then learn the narrator has given Pilar a gun.
key_facts: Checker says he is keeping tabs on everyone and tracking Professor Sonya's phone, and that she has been staying put.
Arthur promises he will run away if there appears to be any danger to them.
Checker suggests the matter may be a job for the authorities, since the bad guys probably cannot make good on the note's threat yet.
Checker says an agency like the NSA would have resources far beyond theirs and could begin putting safeguards in place for the most sensitive government systems.
Checker notes the NSA would be just as likely to recruit Professor Sonya as to throw her in a cell.
Arthur says Sonya never wanted the authorities involved before he stops himself mid-sentence.
Arthur asks for twenty-four hours to contain the problem, and says he will make the call himself if they cannot.
Checker agrees to the twenty-four-hour deadline and hangs up.
Arthur says he does not like any of it, noting that people are trying to kill them and that he worries about Checker and Pilar.
The narrator tells Arthur that Pilar has a gun, which the narrator gave her.
Pilar begged the narrator to teach her to shoot after Arthur would not.
Arthur swears and says the world he wants to live in is not one where his office manager is armed.
The narrator points out the hypocrisy of Arthur, who holds a carry permit.
Arthur asks whether the narrator taught Pilar muzzle safety.
